title: The Mongol Invasion of Japan
description: Summer 1281. Kublai Khan's second invasion fleet arrives off Hakata Bay, where Japanese defenders have spent years building a stone wall along the shoreline. The player commands the samurai defence and must hold the wall and harass the anchored fleet until the late-summer typhoon destroys it.

issues_found: The Yuan invasion fleet — the central object of the scenario, which the player is told to raid and which the typhoon must destroy — is represented by no ships whatsoever. The engine offers TRANSPORT_SHIP, WAR_GALLEY, FIRE_SHIP and DOCK; the 'anchored fleet' is instead two PAVILION_A tents and two flags, so the 'Raid the Anchored Fleet' and typhoon KILL_OBJECT beats have no visible fleet to act on.

Mongol landing force is cavalry-heavy (CAVALRY_ARCHER x9, LIGHT_CAVALRY x4) for a beachhead where the Yuan army was overwhelmingly disembarked infantry and crossbowmen crammed onto a narrow strand; a larger proportion of SPEARMAN/ARCHER and fewer horse would have been closer to the sources.

CLIFF_DEFAULT_3 x480 dominates the map, but Hakata Bay's Genko Borui was built along a low sandy shoreline; the cliff-walled terrain misrepresents the geography that made the stone wall necessary in the first place.

The [Bonus] trigger and its text assert 'Fan Wenhu has fallen!' — Fan Wenhu survived the campaign, abandoned his troops and fled home, and was later disgraced. Rewarding the player for killing him invents a death the sources deny.

Only 19 samurai and 14 archers stand for the assembled Kyushu gokenin levies; the defence reads as a garrison skirmish rather than a mobilized provincial host, and no dock/naval element exists for the Japanese small-boat raiders either.
